dedupe_keys.name: digital future farm digital twin for arable and dairy farming and its elsa assessment wur agrifoodtef

description: Digital Future Farm (DFF) is a Dutch project building digital twin technology and AI-powered decision support for arable and dairy farming, and this case study records its assessment of the ethical, legal and societal aspects (ELSA) of that technology. DFF connects validated farm models with real-time farm data through the open-source MODCOM framework and integrates farm data spaces through the FarmMaps platform, so that tools can predict outcomes such as nutrient flows and environmental impact. It is run by Wageningen University & Research, tasked by the Ministry of Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality to develop the data infrastructure, and supported by the Dutch node of agrifoodTEF, the EU testing and experimentation facility for agri-food, which held an ELSA scan and a Quadruple Helix workshop of farmers, researchers and policymakers at the De Marke agro-innovation centre in Hengelo. Coverage is national, for the Netherlands. The story page is free online. The workshop recommended transparency on data access and use, an API-first approach to interoperability, and fair distribution of financial benefits among data owners. Caveats: the page is a short success story without technical detail or results of the twin itself. For simulation it shows the governance conditions for farm digital twins that couple several models to shared farm data. It is related to the TwinYields case study record in this catalogue, a Finnish farm digital twin.
